text: An SRT file is a numbered list of cues. Each cue is a sequence number, a start-and-end time line using --> , and one or more lines of text, followed by a blank line: 1 00:00:12,000 --> 00:00:15,500 This is the first subtitle. 2 00:00:16,000 --> 00:00:18,200 An

text: SMS finds a subtitle automatically by name-matching : it takes the video's file name, drops the extension, and looks in the same folder for a file with the same base name and a .srt , .sub or .txt extension. If it finds one, it loads it when the video starts.

text: On a clean install SMS starts nothing automatically — you turn on the devices you want. There are two ways to get USB running.

title: Autostart USB (recommended)

title: Start USB now (on demand)

title: MX4SIO (microSD)
text: Play video, audio and pictures from a microSD in an MX4SIO adapter — the headline feature of this SMS build: reliable MX4SIO playback over the PS2 memory-card (SIO2) bus, with its own device icon.

title: What MX4SIO is
text: An MX4SIO adapter takes a microSD card and presents it to the PS2 through the memory-card slot, communicating over the console's SIO2 controller bus (the same bus the pad and memory card use). To SMS the card looks like any other BDM (Block Device Manager) mas

title: Compatibility
text: SMS reads the card through the standard FAT/exFAT layer, so a microSD formatted as FAT32 or exFAT will mount. FAT32 is the safe, universally-compatible choice; exFAT lets you use larger cards and store files bigger than 4 GB. Either way, the media files themse

text: On a fresh install SMS starts nothing automatically — you switch on the devices you want. There are two ways to bring MX4SIO up.

title: Autostart MX4SIO
text: In the settings menu, turn on Autostart MX4SIO . From then on SMS loads the MX4SIO driver at boot and the card is ready to browse as soon as the desktop appears. This is the option to use if MX4SIO is your everyday media source. Your choice is saved with the r

title: Two ways to use the HDD

title: Troubleshooting
text: Fixes for the common SMS problems: video that stutters or won't play, a device that won't appear, SMB shares that won't connect, settings that don't save, and corrupted HD display modes.

title: A video stutters, drops frames, or won't play
text: SMS decodes video in software on the Emotion Engine and uses the PS2's IPU for colour conversion. That is a fixed budget — a file that is too demanding for the console will stutter no matter how fast your storage is. Work through these in order.

title: A storage device doesn't appear
text: If a device you plugged in isn't showing in the top-row device menu, it's almost always one of three things: it isn't started, it isn't formatted the way SMS expects, or it's blocked by a mutual exclusion.

title: An SMB share won't connect
text: SMS speaks the older SMB1 / CIFS network-share protocol. By far the most common reason a share won't connect is that the server no longer accepts SMB1. ✖ Top cause: SMB1 is disabled on the server Modern Windows and Samba ship with SMB1 turned off by default fo

title: Settings don't persist across reboots
text: If your Autostart toggles, network details or playback preferences reset every time you power on, the config isn't being saved — or isn't being found on the next boot.
